Based on the retrieved matches, it appears that PET/CT has a limited role in hepatic staging of Liver Metastases of Colorectal Carcinoma. While PET-CT has higher sensitivity for detecting extrahepatic disease in some anatomic locations, its results are hampered by low Positive Predictive Value (PPV). As a result, only 8% of cases provided additional useful information, with 9% resulting in incorrect and potentially harmful data.

In contrast, multidetector CT (MDCT) provides more comprehensive imaging, which is often considered the gold standard for liver metastases staging. However, MDCT may not be able to detect all extrahepatic disease, especially in patients with high-risk features or those who require selective use of PET/CT.

Therefore, it appears that PET/CT should not be relied upon as a primary tool for preoperative staging of patients with liver metastases of colorectal carcinoma. Instead, multidetector CT may still offer benefits in detecting extrahepatic disease and guiding treatment decisions.
